synopsis: AcrossWAM1.0 studies whether LaWAM's latent-subgoal policy can support explicit backbone interfaces, a smaller multimodal backbone, and an auditable deployment export. A predicted transition latent is decoded into future visual features that condition continuous action generation. The strongest evidence is a paired LIBERO comparison: the compact policy achieves 97.45% versus 98.00% for the larger configuration. Cross-family evidence is limited to adapter execution, and inconsistent RoboTwin entries and parameter labels require clarification. [E02, E03, E09, E12, E13, E15]

problem.text: The authors address implementation coupling between a multimodal policy, its latent world model, and deployment checkpoint. Changing a backbone can alter hidden dimensions, query handling, image arguments, and vocabulary behavior. Their research question is whether an explicit module contract supports compact policies with retained closed-loop performance and verifiably removable training state.

contributions.text: An explicit adapter contract separates transition-query context, action-query context, hidden-size alignment, and training versus inference modules. The latent-subgoal algorithm itself is attributed to LaWAM.
A paired evaluation compares newly trained Qwen3-VL-2B and Qwen3.5-0.8B policies using the same episode initializations.
An export audit checks retained tensors, removed training modules, duplicate aliases, and CPU loading; a separate MiniCPM-V smoke test probes the adapter boundary.

inputs: Current main-view and optional wrist/auxiliary images, language instruction, and optional proprioceptive state. [E03, E05]
Training additionally uses future observations, demonstrated action chunks, and valid state displacements where available. [E04, E06]
outputs: A 32-dimensional predicted transition latent and a spatial future-feature subgoal. [E04, E05]
A continuous chunk of 50 actions spanning 1.2 seconds in the reported configuration. [E06, E18]

steps.name: Learn the transition representation
steps.detail: Frozen DINOv3 encodes current and future observations into patch tokens. A one-query inverse-dynamics Q-Former observes both endpoints and produces a Gaussian transition posterior. A decoder uses latent-conditioned adaptive normalization and gated transformer updates to predict future tokens from current tokens. A masked state-displacement objective grounds the latent in robot motion when state labels exist.

steps.name: Expose backbone-specific processing through an adapter
steps.detail: The backbone processes images, instruction, and two disjoint groups of eight learned queries. Latent-action queries supply transition context; flow queries supply action-generation context. The adapter exposes these slices and accommodates backbone-specific image arguments and hidden dimensions.

steps.name: Predict and decode a policy subgoal
steps.detail: A one-query cross-attention mapper compresses latent-action query states into the predicted transition latent. During training it imitates the frozen inverse-dynamics teacher. At inference the retained decoder combines that prediction with current DINOv3 tokens to produce a spatial future feature without receiving the actual future frame.

steps.name: Generate continuous actions
steps.detail: A Flow-DiT expert conditions on backbone context and concatenated current/predicted-future visual tokens. Its learned vector field transforms Gaussian action noise into an action chunk through numerical integration. Thus the future-feature prediction participates directly in action generation.

training.text: Stage 1 combines future-feature reconstruction, masked state-displacement prediction, and KL regularization. Frozen DINOv3 supplies a stationary feature target; the authors argue that the bottleneck and state supervision encourage action-relevant transitions rather than shared appearance.

Stage 2 combines flow matching, future-subgoal supervision, and latent distillation. In the compact experiment, DINOv3 and the teacher are frozen, while the backbone, mapper, world decoder, and action expert are optimized. The decoder therefore adapts during backbone scaling.

The compact run uses 25,000 training steps. Appendix A specifies two noise samples per batch, gradient clipping at 1.0, AdamW peak learning rates of 10^-4 for the VLM/flow expert and 3×10^-4 for the decoder. The action expert has hidden size 1,024, 16 heads, and 16 layers.

inference.text: Current observations and language drive latent prediction, one-pass world decoding, and action generation with 10 integration steps; optional state appears in the action-conditioning formulation. The inverse-dynamics teacher, state-grounding head, and future observation are absent.

The reported LIBERO success measures closed-loop simulated control. The auxiliary RGB decoder used for the qualitative latent rollout is outside policy inference and success evaluation. The supplied text does not establish how many predicted actions execute before observations are refreshed.

equations.expression: p(a, ĥ_{t+Δ}, z_t | o_t, ℓ, s_t) = p_θ(z_t | o_t, ℓ) p_ω(ĥ_{t+Δ} | h_t, z_t) p_η(a | c_θ, h_t, ĥ_{t+Δ}, s_t), with h_t = f_ψ(o_t).
equations.explanation: Equation (1) separates the language-conditioned transition prior, scene-conditioned world decoder, and action expert. The explicit future feature mediates between intended change and control.

equations.expression: q_ϕ(z_t | h_t, h_{t+Δ}) = N(μ_ϕ, diag(σ_ϕ²)); L_S1 = SmoothL1_{β=0.1}(h̃_{t+Δ}, h_{t+Δ}) + λ_s ||m_s ⊙ (g_ξ(s_t,z_t) − Δs_t)||₂² + β_KL D_KL(q_ϕ || N(0,I)).
equations.explanation: Equations (2) and (5) define the endpoint-conditioned posterior and its training objective. The mask m_s excludes unavailable state dimensions; λ_s and β_KL weight grounding and regularization.

equations.expression: ẑ_t = M_ρ(c_θ^LA); ĥ_{t+Δ} = D_ω(h_t, ẑ_t); L_distill = ||ẑ_t − z_t*||₂²; L_subgoal = ||ĥ_{t+Δ} − h_{t+Δ}||₂².
equations.explanation: Equations (6)–(7) connect the policy's transition prediction to both the frozen teacher target z_t* and the observed future feature. Only the policy prediction and decoder remain necessary at inference.

equations.expression: a_τ = (1−τ)a_0 + τa_1; u_τ = a_1−a_0; L_flow = E[||v_η(a_τ,τ | c_θ,h_t,ĥ_{t+Δ},s_t)−u_τ||₂²]; L_S2 = L_flow + 0.1 L_subgoal + 0.1 L_distill.
equations.explanation: Equations (8)–(10) train a velocity field between Gaussian noise a_0 and normalized demonstrated actions a_1. The displayed auxiliary weights are those of the compact configuration.

results.setting: Four suites, 10 tasks per suite, 50 trials per task; 2,000 matched episode keys per policy, with identical seeds, order, and initializations.
results.metric: Pooled success and exact paired McNemar test
results.value: Reported compact success: 97.45% (1,949/2,000); difference −0.55 percentage points; p = 0.2664.
results.comparison: Qwen3-VL-2B: 98.00% (1,960/2,000). Discordant outcomes: 46 larger-only successes and 35 compact-only successes.
results.interpretation: The observed drop meets the prespecified two-percentage-point engineering criterion. Failure to detect a paired difference does not establish equivalence or statistical non-inferiority, particularly with one checkpoint per backbone.

results.setting: The same paired comparison, with 500 episodes per suite.
results.comparison: Larger model: Long 96.6%; Object 99.2%; Goal 96.8%; Spatial 99.4%.
results.interpretation: The largest observed decline is in Long, at 1.6 percentage points. The aggregate result does not imply uniform retention across task types.

results.setting: Unique-parameter accounting across backbone replacement and deployment export.
results.value: Reported compact raw checkpoint: 1,883.8M; compact deployment export: 1,472.6M; reported reduction against the 2B reference: 42.4%.
results.comparison: The 2,555.2M reference is labeled deployable in Table 2 but raw in Table 3.
results.interpretation: The compact export count is consistently reported. The reference's raw/deploy labeling needs clarification before treating the percentage as independently reconciled inference-only accounting. Parameter reduction does not establish latency or memory improvement.

results.setting: Author-reported state-dictionary audit and production CPU loading.
results.value: 1,078 retained tensors bitwise identical; 321 training-only keys representing 411.1M parameters removed; 718 removed alias keys reconstructible bitwise.
results.comparison: Exported state compared with the source checkpoint.
results.interpretation: This supports checkpoint-state preservation and CPU materialization. It does not establish exported-policy behavior on an accelerator or in the simulator; those checks were not included.

results.metric: Input compatibility, query influence, hidden-size alignment, and optimization behavior
results.value: Reported compatible image/embedding inputs, query-dependent outputs, automatic hidden-size alignment, and decreasing training loss.
results.comparison: Exercises the adapter contract beyond the two Qwen configurations.
results.interpretation: This tests software execution. It supplies no cross-family manipulation success rate or evidence of frozen-decoder transfer.

results.setting: Two-task RoboTwin diagnostic changing left versus right; adherence measured among completed conflicting-instruction placements.
results.value: Guidance variant adherence: 93/185 (50.3%), versus 52/190 (27.4%); Fisher exact p = 1.0×10^-5.
results.comparison: Conflicting-instruction collapse: 38.3% versus 36.7%, p = 0.74. Non-conflicting collapse rises from 1% to 10%.
results.interpretation: Improved adherence among completed placements accompanies worse completion behavior on non-conflicting instructions. This conditional diagnostic is not an aggregate RoboTwin benchmark result.

limitations.text: Table 1 prints AcrossWAM1.0 RoboTwin Clean/Randomized values of 92.09/89.12, whereas Sections 4.2 and 5 and Appendix C explicitly restrict its benchmark evidence to LIBERO. This unresolved source contradiction prevents accepting those entries as established AcrossWAM1.0 results.

The experiment changes both Qwen generation and nominal backbone size while retraining the decoder and other policy modules. It establishes performance for these configurations, rather than isolating parameter count or frozen-interface transfer as the causal factor.

No reported intervention removes the subgoal, disables distillation, or freezes the decoder under an otherwise matched comparison. Consequently, these experiments do not newly establish the control benefit of the inherited latent-subgoal mechanism.

The authors identify missing training-seed replication, compact-policy latency and peak-memory measurements, cross-family closed-loop evaluation, and accelerator/simulator testing of the export. Published LaWAM robot and latency results are not new AcrossWAM1.0 evidence.
The auxiliary-decoded latent rollout is qualitative. Its caption's claims about preserved structure and accumulating blur could not be independently assessed from the supplied text.

reproduction.text: The authors describe accompanying code, configurations, evaluators, paired statistics, and export-verification artifacts. Their availability and behavior were not checked in this reading, and no experiment was reproduced.

Reproduction needs the exact backbone and Stage-1 checkpoints, training data and preprocessing, action normalization, query/vocabulary handling, and matched LIBERO episode keys. The supplied text gives losses and several optimizer settings, but omits data mixture/size, batch size, hardware budget, and action-execution/replanning schedule.

A focused portability test would compare frozen versus trainable world decoders under matched training and evaluation, then repeat across backbone families and training seeds. Separately, running the exported checkpoint through the accelerator and simulator would test the deployment boundary beyond tensor equality.

reasoning.text: The recorded Dual-system classification is supported by explicit boundaries among the policy adapter, retained world decoder, and separately conditioned action expert; joint optimization does not make them a single predictive model. IDM is supported by the endpoint-conditioned inverse-dynamics teacher that defines the transition bottleneck, with an essential qualification: that teacher is training-only. Inference predicts a latent, decodes a future feature, and generates actions with Flow-DiT rather than executing the inverse-dynamics encoder. Latent prediction and visual-subgoal conditioning are demonstrated architectural properties; the real-time-control tag remains unverified because compact latency is absent.

discussionQuestions: How much compact-policy performance depends on adapting the world decoder, and would a frozen decoder survive a genuinely different backbone family? [E07, E13]
Would directional adherence improve when evaluated jointly with completion, rather than conditioned on completed placements? [E14]
Which artifacts reconcile the contradictory RoboTwin row and the larger checkpoint's raw/deploy labels? [E12, E15]

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title, author block, and arXiv version line
evidence.detail: The title and authors Yafei Zhang and Nan Wu match the catalog identity. The supplied artifact identifies itself as arXiv:2608.29937v1, dated 30 August 2026.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 1–3, Abstract, Section 1 contributions, and Section 3.1
evidence.detail: The paper attributes latent-subgoal learning to LaWAM and presents its own contribution as modular interfaces, backbone scaling, and deployment verification.
The formulation specifies observations, language, optional state, a transition latent, frozen visual features, a future-feature decoder, and a conditioned action expert.
Stage 1 uses frozen DINOv3, a one-query Gaussian inverse-dynamics posterior with latent dimension 32, latent-modulated decoding, masked state grounding, future-feature loss, and KL regularization.
Eight latent-action and eight flow queries have separate roles. A cross-attention mapper predicts the teacher-aligned latent, which the retained decoder converts into a supervised future feature.

Flow matching interpolates Gaussian noise and normalized action chunks. The expert conditions on backbone and current/future visual context; the configuration uses 50 actions, a 1.2-second horizon, 10 integration steps, and auxiliary weights of 0.1.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Section 3.6 and opening of Section 4; PDF p. 6, Section 4.1
evidence.detail: Inference excludes future frames, the inverse-dynamics encoder, and state-grounding head. Compact training freezes DINOv3 and the teacher while optimizing the decoder and policy modules. LaWAM's published control and latency results are explicitly inherited references.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Section 4.1, Models and training, Benchmarks, and Statistics
evidence.detail: The compact model trains for 25,000 steps. Evaluation uses 50 trials for each of 10 tasks in four suites, identical episode keys and initializations, a two-point retention criterion, and one checkpoint per backbone.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 2, pooled columns; PDF p. 6, Section 4.3
evidence.detail: The larger and compact policies achieve 1,960/2,000 and 1,949/2,000 successes. Larger-only and compact-only successes number 46 and 35; the reported exact McNemar p-value is 0.2664.

evidence.location: PDF p. 12, Appendix B, Table 4, Long/Object/Goal/Spatial rows
evidence.detail: Larger versus compact success rates are 96.6/95.0, 99.2/99.4, 96.8/96.8, and 99.4/98.6 percent, respectively, with 500 episodes per suite.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Section 4.5; PDF p. 8, Table 3
evidence.detail: The export audit reports 1,078 unchanged retained tensors, 321 removed training-only keys covering 411.1M parameters, 718 reconstructible aliases, and successful CPU loading. Table 3 lists compact raw/export counts of 1,883.8M/1,472.6M and a 42.4% reduction against the larger reference.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 2, Qwen3-VL-2B deploy-parameters cell; PDF p. 8, Table 3, first row and caption
evidence.detail: Table 2 calls 2,555.2M the larger model's deployable count. Table 3 labels the same count a raw policy and defines raw as including training-only modules.

MiniCPM-V 4.6 passes an author-reported adapter forward/backward test with query influence, compatible image arguments, hidden-size alignment, and decreasing loss. Its vocabulary requires explicit resizing/freezing treatment; no manipulation result is claimed.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 8–9, Section 4.7; PDF p. 9, Section 5
evidence.detail: The two-task language diagnostic reports adherence of 52/190 versus 93/185, Fisher p=1.0×10^-5, conflicting collapse of 36.7% versus 38.3% with p=0.74, and non-conflicting collapse increasing from 1% to 10%.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 1, AcrossWAM1.0 row; PDF p. 6, Section 4.2 final paragraph; PDF p. 9, Section 5; PDF p. 12, Appendix C
evidence.detail: The table assigns AcrossWAM1.0 RoboTwin values of 92.09 and 89.12. The surrounding text says those columns are not filled with inherited or diagnostic results and restricts verified closed-loop benchmark evidence to LIBERO.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 6–7, Section 4.4; PDF p. 8, Figure 2 caption, text only
evidence.detail: A held-out trajectory is autoregressively predicted for 33 steps and rendered with an auxiliary RGB decoder solely for interpretation. The decoder is absent from policy inference and success evaluation; the caption describes increasing long-horizon blur.

evidence.location: PDF p. 9, Section 5; PDF p. 12, Appendix C
evidence.detail: Explicit gaps include training-seed replication, frozen cross-family decoder transfer, cross-family control, compact latency and peak memory, and accelerator/simulator export validation.

Implementation settings include hidden size 1,024, latent dimension 32, eight queries of each type, a 16-layer/16-head expert, two noise samples per batch, clipping at 1.0, and module-specific AdamW peak learning rates.

The authors state that an accompanying repository contains model and training code, configurations, evaluators, paired statistical tests, and machine-readable export verification. These external materials were not supplied for inspection.
